records.summary: The sudden electricity price increase in Europe in 2021 raised concerns about the ability of power markets to withstand energy price shocks without compromising climate goals. This study shows that countries with larger shares of decarbonized electricity were not more exposed to natural gas price shocks.

records.title: Assessing timber trade networks and supply chains in Brazil
records.summary: The illegal timber trade is one of the primary drivers of deforestation in Brazil. A study now analyses timber trade networks and supply chains to identify actors operating contrary to the regulations and continuing to support illegal timber trade.

records.title: The future of large-scale solar interfacial desalination
records.summary: Solar interfacial desalination could enable the sustainable production of freshwater, but scale-up remains challenging. Now, analysis of the efficiency and costs of a large-scale interfacial desalination system operating outdoors over nearly four months suggests that scale-up is associated with high capital investment and a lower water production rate compared with laboratory-scale devices.

records.title: Viability and desirability of financing conservation in Africa through fire management
records.summary: Adopting early dry season fires has been proposed as a means of generating sufficient carbon revenues to pay for conservation in Africa. However, the climatic impact thereof is deeply questionable and may have unforeseen detrimental effects.

records.title: Data-driven strategies to improve nitrogen use efficiency of rice farming in South Asia
records.summary: Overuse of nitrogen fertilizer in crop cultivation can lead to environmental pollution necessitating strategies to optimize nitrogen use efficiency (NUE). This study examines data from more than 31,000 farmer fields across South Asia to identify opportunities for improving NUE in rice cropping systems.

records.title: Regional patterns of wild animal hunting in African tropical forests
records.summary: Wildlife hunting can support diets and socio-economic well-being in communities around the world, but overexploitation can have cascading ecosystem effects. This study examines socio-cultural, economic and landscape factors associated with wildlife hunting in tropical forests in Africa.

records.title: Industrial-scale sustainable rare earth mining enabled by electrokinetics
records.summary: Greener mining technologies for rare earth elements (REEs) extraction are of vital importance to creating a sustainable REEs supply. Here the authors achieve industrial-scale REEs mining with reduced environmental footprint using an electrokinetic mining technique.

records.title: Large-scale implementation of solar interfacial desalination
records.summary: Despite its enormous potential to address water scarcity, solar interfacial desalination remains at only the research level. Here the authors scale up its implementation and identify the key technical and cost issues that must be addressed to accelerate market adoption of this promising technology.

records.title: Changes in global fluvial sediment concentrations and fluxes between 1985 and 2020
records.summary: Suspended sediments in river networks are a critical pathway for material and nutrient transport from land to the oceans, but global monitoring is challenging. Satellite records for the past three decades document an increase in sediment delivery, driven by climate and land-cover change.

records.title: Diversified cropping systems with limited carbon accrual but increased nitrogen supply
records.summary: Sustainable and regenerative agriculture often employs diverse systems of crop rotation to reduce environmental impacts and sequester carbon. A long-term field study, however, reveals a trade-off between soil organic carbon storage and nitrogen supply.

records.title: The potential land-use impacts of bio-based plastics and plastic alternatives
records.summary: Bio-based plastics have gained attention as a potentially sustainable way to reduce fossil fuel-based plastic demand and store carbon. However, large-scale adoption of bio-based alternatives could have a substantial impact on land use, including deforestation.
